subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Centrifugal Pumps: Spinning Fluid Outward
description: A quick win: understand Centrifugal Pumps: Spinning Fluid Outward.

hook.text: Spin a bucket of water and it pushes to the outside. Pumps do the same.

buildup.text: A spinning impeller flings fluid outward, converting speed to pressure.

discovery.text: The volute casing slows the fluid down, trading velocity for pressure.

twist.text: Run one dry and the impeller overheats fast — water is the coolant.

climax.text: Most water supply and HVAC systems use centrifugal pumps. They're everywhere.

punchline.text: Spin fluid fast, then slow it down. That's a pump.

quiz.question: How does a centrifugal pump build pressure?
options: Pistons push fluid through a narrow valve
A spinning impeller flings fluid outward; the casing converts speed to pressure
A vacuum at the inlet pulls fluid through the system
